# Optimization plan - what to take from Flycast

Review of Flycast (`E:\Users\Matteo\Desktop\Dreamcast\flycast`) against our tree,
Reicast and Minicast. Written 2026-09-23. Flycast is an allowed reference from
this date (Matt).

Rule: every item ends with a hardware test on Matt's PS3. Never RPCS3.
Status: `[ ]` open, `[~]` active, `[x]` done (HW validated), `[!]` blocked.

Flycast is little-endian only. Check every ported line for byte order.

- Row RENDERER > Near Plane Cap (`NearCap`, OLD / WIDE, live, default OLD).
  WIDE with Depth Float ON: a 1/W up to 2^44, not 2^20 (reicast's 1024 x
  1024), can set the near plane. Depth Float OFF keeps 2^20: a Z24 step is
  2^-24 / n in 1/W. The reject of inf and NaN stays.
- Code: `ps3/spu/spe_bell.h` has the decode option `TAOPT_INVW_WIDE` (128)
  and the caps `INVW_CAP_OLD` (0x49800000) and `INVW_CAP_WIDE` (0x55800000).
  `ta_opts_now()` sets the bit at each list init when the row is WIDE and
  Depth Float is ON. `track_inv_w()` (PPU replay), `track_w()` (`spe_dec.c`)
  and `draw_scene()` (the background's 1/W, the fallback test) pick the cap
  by the bit; `draw_scene()` takes WIDE only with FLOAT depth.
- Why 2^44: Flycast's largest per-game depth scale (1e8, NHL 2K2) orders a
  1/W up to 1.7e13. FLOAT keeps 16 mantissa bits at any n; the far end (1/W
  1e-9) stays a normal float up to a cap of about 2^96.

- The game's loaders (8C057780 and 13 more call sites) find a code chunk
  ('AREA', 'SYSP') in data already in RAM (8C09C5A0), run the cache
  routine, then call the chunk's first word (`jsr @r10`) and relocate its
  pointer table. A chunk that CPU stores placed (the disc has 450 .GZ
  files) does not reach the DMA code drop: theory, not proven.
- The I-cache rule: a CCR write that turns the I-cache on (ICE 0 -> 1)
  clears the JIT code cache, as ICI does (`dc/sh4/ccn.cpp`). In the 24
  boots of 2026-10-17 the other games turn the I-cache on 3-5 times, all at
  boot; Shenmue II 16-18 times a session. Log: a `recSh4: cache clear` line
  right before each `CCN: I-cache enabled` line.
- A DMA that writes a 32-byte line of RAM that compiled code reads clears
  the code cache: the GD-ROM DMA, the PVR DMA to RAM, the G2 DMAs (AICA
  read, EXT1, EXT2) and the Maple replies. Line `[jdma] <DMA> DMA to
  <addr>, <n> bytes, over compiled code (<k> lines of 32 bytes from <line>,
  <m> pages opened): code cache clear #<n>, <p> pages open`, then the usual
  `recSh4: cache clear` line.
- A 1 KB page hit again within 60 vblanks opens (Flycast's unprotected
  page): its blocks check their first and last opcode at entry and leave
  the map, so its DMAs clear no more.
- Not with the MMU JIT; not CPU stores (the known-SMC list stays).
- PC (WSL): `misc/jdma_check` PASS, `mutate.py` 34 of 34; gd2_check,
  gdasync_check, g2dma_check, maple_check (with new DMA report checks),
  sysgate, timebase, clock, flash and cold checks PASS; the new mutants of
  gd2 (4), gdasync (1), g2dma (4) and maple (5) are caught. The I-cache
  rule: its line is pinned in jdma_check (35 of 35 mutants), mmu_check
  PASS. No new build warning. `.got` 0xFF20 of 0x10000 (0xE0 bytes left),
  0 r2off.
- Risk: a DMA into a line of code that runs, at intervals of more than 1 s,
  clears the cache each time (a short stall at each clear, not a fault). A
  game that turns the I-cache on often clears at each turn.

**P101 fallback per block and P102 8C BASE REG (`OPTIMIZATION_POTENTIAL.md`
P101, P102), built 2026-10-17 (Matt: "Go for it. Also, while you're at it:
Check for a faster memory. And the 4-5 op sequence ..."). Package of 17:37
(`build/notdc_ps3.pkg`, 1787888 bytes) = the package of 16:23 + this. Not
committed. JIT SHORT FORMS: OFF / ON / 8C PREFIX / 8C BASE REG (new), set
before boot. No HW run yet.**
- 8C PREFIX and 8C BASE REG: a block whose cold paths see RAM 4096 times
  (another mirror, a junk upper half; MMIO and the store queue do not
  count) is compiled again with the 2-op guard, after a full cache clear
  between blocks. Line `[jopt] 8C PREFIX fallback #N: block X ...` each
  time; `[jopt] ... fallback blocks= demotes=`.
- 8C BASE REG: r11 holds the block's bias; a 32-bit load or store with no
  displacement is 4 words (`rldicl; cmpldi; bne; lwzx rD,A,r11`). Pairs
  and folded displacements stay at 5. Needs JIT TA SLOT OFF (else 8C
  PREFIX, with a `[jitcfg]` line).
- Faster memory: the DC memory already sits in 1 MB pages (the PSL1GHT
  heap); nothing faster to take.
- PC (WSL): fmem_check PASS (`mutate.py` 45 of 45), sched_check PASS (47
  of 47), the checks that read the changed files PASS. No new build
  warning. `.got` 0xFEF8: 0x108 bytes left.
- Risk: r11 must hold the bias wherever a base access runs; a miss shows
  as wrong data, a crash or a freeze. A fallback clear stutters once.
- HW run 10 (same log, Crazy Taxi, 8C BASE REG, package of 17:37): the SH4
  thread hung after START at the title (t=93 s, pc 0C08195E, no fault
  line); 16 fallbacks before it, most in the boot code (0xAC blocks).
  Cause: a C call on a path that runs only at times (`pref`'s store-queue

  Fixed: package of 17:59 (1787888 bytes); the HW steps below stand.

**P99 and P100, the heavy-scene stall work (`OPTIMIZATION_POTENTIAL.md` P99,
P100), built 2026-10-17 (Matt: "Let's go with option 2 and 3."). Package of
15:05 (`build/notdc_ps3.pkg`, 1786160 bytes) = commit 311d430 + P96 + P87 +
GD-ROM Timing HOST + P97 + P98 + this. Not committed. Three rows on JIT
SPEED, all default OFF and set before boot. No HW run yet.**
- Why (the answer to "What are our options", 2026-10-17): in heavy scenes
  the game code runs at about 1 PPC instruction every 4-6 cycles; the
  vertex loops at about 1 a cycle are only 3-5% of the time. Theory, not
  measured: code-cache and L2 misses (option 2) and in-order pipeline
  waits (option 3). Option 1, the measure-first package, was not taken.

**P96 GD-ROM Read Ahead and P87 JIT TA SLOT, for Crazy Taxi's slow parts
(`OPTIMIZATION_POTENTIAL.md` P96, P87), built 2026-10-16 (Matt: "Do option 2
and 3. Do they break other games?"). Package of 22:42 (`build/notdc_ps3.pkg`,

- Why: Crazy Taxi's slow parts (14-25K vertices, 86-94%) are SH4-bound. In
  today's 16 slow seconds the SH4 waited 73 ms/s for disc reads (GD-ROM
  Timing FIXED), and the TA store-queue path took ~12% (1.0-1.2M flushes a
  second, ~215 ns each).
- Row GD-ROM > GD-ROM Read Ahead (`GdReadAhead`, live): after each fill the
  worker reads the next 64 data sectors (batches of 32) into a ring of 128;
  a fill the ring holds is a RAM copy. The `[gdr]` line ends with `fills N
  seq N dra 0|1 hit N read N/N ms(max)` (seq: fills that start where the
  last one ended; this count is there with the row OFF too).
- Row JIT SPEED > JIT TA SLOT (`JitTaSlot`, set before boot): the stores of
  a TA record also go into the TA buffer's next record, so the flush reads
  nothing back (P87 has the design). Lines: `[taslot] ns: ...` at every
  boot (the probe: the read-back's own wait), `[taslot] hit= copy=
  records=` each second with the row ON, `[jitcfg] ... taslot=`.

  fuzz alone; two equal-code mutants left out); `misc/ramsq_check` PASS with

**P95, Rez: the RTT and the next list wait for the render thread
(`OPTIMIZATION_POTENTIAL.md` P95), built 2026-10-16 (Matt: "Let's go with
option 1."). Package of 21:00 (`build/notdc_ps3.pkg`, 1764720 bytes) =
commit 944c740 + this; committed by Matt as 311d430. HW run 1 (below): Rez's heavy parts
85% -> 100%. Both rows default ON since the package of 21:00 (Matt: "Sure,
set them on by default.").**
- Cause, from Rez's long HW run (`ps3log_p89_run1.txt` lines 59208-74010):
  each frame has a main scene and a 256x256 render to texture (RTT).
  `rth_run(JOB_RTT)` blocked the SH4 until the render thread ended the main
  scene before it, then until the RTT was drawn, read back and copied. In
  the 29 heartbeats of t=412-440 s (25-33K vertices, 73-88%, 21-26 frames
  a second, no sleep): the SH4 waits in the RTT 21 times (16 with the
  render thread on the main scene); the SH4 runs game code 8 times, each
  time with the render thread idle. Render busy 67-72% (~30 ms a frame).
  The SPU decoder waits for the render thread before a list reset 23-25
  times a second (25-30% of its time): the RTT list and the main list
  share one TA context. With no RTT (t=465-516 s), 16-20K vertices run at
  100% with 100-260 ms/s of sleep.
- Row OUTPUT > RTT Async (`RttAsync`, live, default OFF): an RTT that finds
  a job in flight waits in a second job slot (`s_q_*`), and the SH4 runs
  on. When the job ends, the render thread takes the RTT at once (the slot
  stays busy), so no later job passes it. A second RTT waits until the
  first takes the slot. `rth_wait_decode()` and the slot picks also see the
  waiting RTT's context.
- Row OUTPUT > TA Context Split (`TaCtxSplit`, live, default OFF): a list
  init on a context that a job holds (in flight or waiting) moves the TA's
  address to another slot (`ctx_move()`): one with no address first, then
  one whose list a STARTRENDER took (new field `posted`); never a slot a
  job holds or the last replayed one. The old slot keeps its stream and
  lists for its job and loses its address. No free slot: the old wait.
- Log: `[rttq] async= split= | rtt queued= direct= sh4 wait N ms/s | ctx
  moves= full=` in each stats window with a row ON or an RTT; `[outcfg]`
  at boot has `RttAsync` and `TaCtxSplit`.
- PC (WSL): `misc/rttq_check` (new): the job slot, the waiting RTT, the
  waits, the slot picks and ListInit, cut from `ps3_rend.cpp`, run on
  pthreads against a model (6000 frames, 4 seeds: ~12.5K jobs, 1.5-1.9K
  moves, 150-230 with no free slot, rows and Frame Drop changed every 37
  frames, a part with the render thread off). The model checks job order,
  the stream of each job up to its replay, the lists up to the end of its
  draw, the registers of each draw, the blocking RTT with the row OFF, no
  move with the row OFF, no wait at a list init with a free slot, no move
  onto a list no STARTRENDER took, the redraw of the last list, the counts
  of the `[rttq]` line. `mutate.py`: 44 of 44. No build warning. The 22
  other checks that read the changed files PASS (idleauto_check names the
  last three lines of `k_live_opts`: the new line is before them).
- `.got` 0xFB80 of 0x10000 (was 0xFB10).

**Garou's texture churn (`OPTIMIZATION_POTENTIAL.md` P93, row Tex Recycle),
built 2026-10-16 (Matt: "Ok, apply the Garou fixes, and we can consider
this session closed and a SUCCESS."). Package of 16:57
(`build/notdc_ps3.pkg`, 1764208 bytes) = the package of 14:25 + this. Not
committed. The row is OFF by default; no HW run yet.**
- Ways 2 and 3 of the read-only investigation (the P89 block below, Garou
  bullets): reuse an evicted texture for a new one of its size; in ps3gl, a
  new texture name gets its pool entry at glGenTextures.
- Row DRAW COST > Tex Recycle (`TexRecycle`, OFF / ON, live, default OFF).
  It acts on both parts:
  - `ps3/ps3_tex.cpp`: an evicted texture with no mip chain goes to a list
    of spares (at most 256 and 16 MB) and is not deleted. A new texture of
    the same size and layout (mirror, YUV) takes the oldest spare that was
    evicted 2 frames before or earlier, and its texels go into that RSX
    memory: no glGenTextures, no ps3gl pool scan, no rsxMemalign. The wait
    is ps3gl's: `ps3gl_begin_frame` waits for the frame 2 frames back, so
    the RSX no longer samples the spare. Spares not taken in 120 frames
    are deleted, and all of them when the row goes OFF.
  - `ps3/ps3gl/ps3gl_textures.c`, bit `PS3GL_FAST_GEN` (set by the row in
    `rth_job_draw`): glGenTextures takes the pool entry, so the first bind
    finds the name in the table (Tex Bind Table) and not by a scan of 4096
    entries. The scan for a free entry starts at a hint, which is kept on
    every path and finds the entry that the scan from 0 finds.
- Log: `[texfmt] ... | spares reused= put= held=` each window, `[tex]
  recycle ON`, `[costcfg] ... TexRecycle=`.
- Expected in Garou (estimate from the fit of the P89 block): a new
  texture that takes a spare costs about a re-upload (20 us), not 110 us;
  evictions cost about 100 ms/s of the render thread in fights and 300 ms/s
  in the 3.4K scene now. The cache still evicts (1024 slots; more slots was
  way 4, not picked).

  frozen files with the row OFF, now with churn pools (an evicted texture
  is freed). Model: 6 seeds, churn pools of 3 colliding groups, every bind
  texel by texel, and no texture name takes another texture within 2
  frames of its last bind (422-803 such takes a seed). `misc/glpath_check`
  PASS: rows OFF give the old RSX calls (10 seeds); every mix of the 3 bits
  holds the RSX registers of bits 0, and the mixes without the compares
  make the same RSX calls; a new texture
  takes the first free pool entry, and has its entry before the bind only
  with the bit; 20 source lines. Mutants: tex3 74 of 74 (7 new; the text of
  "anisotropic parameter dropped" was stale since bundle 14 and is
  repaired), glpath 89 of 89 (8 new). Also PASS: chd, clock, flash, fschg,
  fullmmu, idleauto, interp, maple, mmu, pad, rtt, screen, sys20, timebase,
  jit8, sysgate, constprop, div32, exit, sqstore, tcopy, ramsq, spepix,

- The rule: the 4-opcode tail block of Kamui's vsync wait `do { hook(7);
  [hook(12);] count--; } while (vbl == old && count);` ends the timeslice,
  as an entry of our list does. It acts with JIT SPEED > JIT IDLE HASH ON
  (the default); OFF turns it off. It matches the code of the whole loop,
  from the `jsr` to the tail's `bf`, at any address (`idle_kamui[]`,
  `idle_kamui_form()` in `dc/sh4/rec_v2/idle_hash.h`; `dec_idle_hash()`
  calls it when no list holds the block). It reads back from the block's
  last word, so it reads code before a block only when the block is a tail.
- Three forms: hook 7 (14 opcodes: Capcom vs. SNK 2, Spider-Man, Project
  Justice, Power Stone 2, Donald Duck, Rayman 2, Re-Volt), hooks 7 and 12
  (16: Ikaruga, Rez), the same with other registers (16: Quake III Arena).
  The `[idle] code` dumps of the HW logs and the 27 disc images on the PC
  hold no other form (the images also: Ecco, Dead or Alive 2, Looney Tunes,
  Border Down, Sonic Shuffle, Phantasy Star Online Ver. 2). A looser scan
  (the same tail with a `mov #7,r4` before it) found nothing more.
- Capcom vs. SNK 2's address entry 8C21A2EE is removed from our list: the
  rule covers that block with the same action (one slice).
- The hooks, read from the disc images: Ikaruga and Rez never set hook 7 or
  12 (they set 0, 2, 5, 8, 11), so both are the library's empty default.
  Capcom vs. SNK 2 and Power Stone 2 reset hook 7 to the default.
  Spider-Man sets hook 7 to a switch into a background task (8C03D000 ->
  8C0466FC) when its flag 8C059C2C is set; in that phase the task runs
  once a slice in the wait.

  - Garou's texture thrash, read only (Matt: "Yes, do it."), nothing built:
    - The game binds 590-833 different textures a frame (`[spetex]
      hashed`), small 4-bit palette sprite tiles. Our cache
      (`ps3/ps3_tex.cpp`) has 1024 slots, and a new texture may only take
      one of 8 neighbouring slots (`CACHE_SLOTS`, `CACHE_PROBE`). `live` is
      815-890 in fights and 982-1024 (full) in the 3.4K scene, so a new
      texture evicts one used in the last 4 frames (97-100% of the
      evictions), which then comes back.
    - Cost on the render thread, a fit over 6 windows of `tex split
      decode` against the counts: about 110 us a new texture, about 20 us
      a re-upload of changed texels. A new texture runs ps3gl's
      glBindTexture of a new name (a full scan of the 4096-entry pool, then
      a scan for a free entry) and rsxMemalign (PSL1GHT's first-fit list,
      block headers in RSX memory, `ppu/librt/heap.c`); the old texture's
      rsxFree comes at the next frame start.
    - Per second: fights about 145 ms of decode time, about 100 ms of it
      from evictions; the 3.4K scene about 350 ms, about 300 from
      evictions (2800 a second). Texel changes (animation or palettes):
      2200-2700 re-uploads a second, about 50 ms; those are real changes.
    - Ways (Matt picks): (1) more cache slots (2048 or more; RSX memory
      grows with the live count, so a memory cap with it); (2) reuse the
      evicted texture and its RSX memory for a new one of the same size
      (no delete, no pool scans, no heap walk; every game with churn); (3)
      ps3gl: a new name gets its pool entry at glGenTextures, so its first
      bind does not scan 4096 entries; (4) later, the palette lookup in the
      shader (one texture for all palettes, Flycast's way).
    - Also seen: Garou's fights run the Shinobi task loop (block
      8C015E70, the same 4 words as the Sonic Shuffle and Border Down task
      entries) at 80-100K turns a second; JIT TASK IDLE's list is bound to
      those two games' addresses, so it does not act in Garou.
    - Scope of ways 1 and 2 (the reuse and the ps3gl pool entry; Matt:
      "Can you check if 1 and 2 will affect Alpha 3, as well?"): they act
      only on new textures. Street Fighter Alpha 3 (this log, lines
      16498-20214): 33-53 textures a frame, at most 159 live, 0 evictions,

- The loop (loop A), Kamui's vsync wait at 8C21A2A0: it reads the vblank
  count at 8C3DC5E4 (the VBLANK_IN handler 8C21AA46 adds 1), then calls
  hook 7 and counts a timeout down from 0x100000 until the count changes.
  Hook 7 is the empty function 8C216D40 (the game resets it to the
  default at start, and nothing else sets it). The turn writes the
  timeout counter, so JIT IDLE SKIP never skips it.
  - Reicast's list holds this loop: its "IKA, HH" entries are the hook
    call (8C217FE0) and its return, and its last entry is the counter
    block (8C21A2DE), but with a typo (`">1:` for `">:1:`), so it never
    matches. Our own list (row JIT IDLE HASH) has no entry for it.
  - The same loop, byte for byte, is in 8 other games of the logs:
    Spider-Man (up to 3.4M turns a second), Project Justice (1.2M),
    Power Stone 2 (1.2M), Ikaruga (1.1M), Rez (1.0M), Donald Duck (72K),
    Rayman 2 (58K), Quake III Arena (12K; Rez and Quake III call hook 12
    too).

  timeslice, so the loop runs one turn a slice. The emulated time of the

    calls `do_sqw_nommu` at each PREF: 92-94 instructions, 12 TOC loads,

    115 ns (IPC about 0.3). In Ikaruga and Rez (AT = 1) the old chain
    costs 23-31% of the thread (P74).
  - Cause 2, the game's own vertex code. SA2's loop 8C141BBA is 161 JIT
    instructions a vertex now: JIT SQ COPY puts all 5 store-queue stores
    inline (the old build had 5 cold entries a turn). Each `fmov @r2+` pays
    its own RAM check (4 a vertex), the two fschg cancel (8 instructions).
  - Cause 3, the sound SPU syncs (SA2). Only G2 DMA writes hit (`hits/s
    sh4 0 dma 445-576 arm 0`), the music feed. At + SAMPLE SYNC each hit
    syncs with no test: 45-86 syncs a second, 0.5-2.5 ms each, a busy spin
    (`wait_tail`, `ps3/ps3_arm_spe.cpp:83`). Estimates from the counters,
    not logged: most of a sync is the ARM7 SPU waiting for the sound SPU,
    whose DSP (64K-word ring through a 16 KB cache) costs about 5.9 us a
    sample; 44-74% of the syncs come from the stale flag.

      - What it does: a PREF to the store queue without the MMU runs the
        common case of do_sqw_nommu's flat path as 55 inline instructions
        (`ps3/ps3_jit_ta.h`, `emit_ta_flush`; 51 with no SPE): the target
        test (QACR0 or QACR1 by address bit 5 says area 4, no YUV or VRAM
        address bits, the gate word open), room in s_ta's raw buffer, `dcbz`
        at each new 128-byte line, the 32-byte copy (4 ld + 4 std), raw_used
        += 32, a count, the FSM entry of the PCW. The old path had a C call
        of 92-94 instructions with 12 TOC loads.
      - The rare cases leave by two cold calls: before the copy the old
        target (do_sqw_nommu, or _frame with TA Peak Frame: RAM, VRAM and
        YUV flushes, no room, no buffer, a closed gate), after it
        `ps3ta_jit_finish` (a TAS_SLOW entry or a due SPE batch: sqw_finish
        without its count). FlushCold kinds 11 and 12. A block takes at most
        8 inline flushes (`TAJ_BLOCK_SITES`); a PREF after them keeps the
        call, so a block grows by about 2 KB at most (ngen_Compile keeps 16 KB).
      - `ps3/ps3_rend.cpp`: `g_ta_jit` (gate word, count); `ta_jit_gate()`
        at each `ta_gate_set` and after the in-game menu (TA SQ Direct is
        live); `ps3ta_jit_addr()` at the latch, with the encoding rules of
        `ps3/ps3_ta_inline.h` and the raw buffers on 128-byte lines (else
        `[tajit] JIT TA INLINE stays off: ...`); VBlank adds the inline count
        to TaCalls; set_ta_context notes the raw peak of the stream it leaves
        (the inline flush notes no peak per record).

- Why not RAM: the PS3 runs JIT code only from the `.text` array (HW probe
  2026-09-20: code in `.bss`, `malloc` and lv2 memory faulted). A RAM copy
  to restore at a switch would not help either: Donald Duck flushes its
  I-cache at each load, which clears all code before the second switch.
- What changed: a switch no longer clears the code cache. A block bills
  its cycles with one word at its start (`addi` or `addic.` of r29 to
  itself, the cycles as the immediate); the code around it does not
  depend on the idle rule (`cycle_poll_needed` reads only the block end).
  - The decoder's bill is a function now, `dec_bill(rule, cycles, max)`
    (the same code as before). It also gives each block both AUTO bills,
    `bill_x3` and `bill_x30` (`dc/sh4/rec_v2/decoder.h`).
  - Under AUTO, `ngen_Compile` notes each compiled block: the address of
    its bill word (`s_bill_insn`, taken in `ngen_Begin`) and both bills.
    A table of 131072 entries (1 MB, allocated at the first note); a code
    cache clear empties it.
  - A switch rewrites the immediate of each noted word
    (`idle_bill_word`: only an `addi`/`addic.` of a register to itself;
    the driver also wants r29), then syncs that line to the I-cache. A
    full table falls back to the cache clear.
  - Log: `[idle-auto] N of M blocks billed again in X ms (K words no
    bill)` after each switch line.

    compiled: the store queue area test in the block, then a C call
    (`jmmu_pref`, `jx_pref`); a fault leaves by the block's exception
    exit, SPC = the pref. IFB: each pref runs on the MMU interpreter, as
    before.
  - MMU ASID JTC OFF / ON (`MmuAsidJtc`, with MMU Model FAST only): the
    JTC of the 8 last ASIDs is kept (32 KB each; the least recently used
    goes). A switch to a kept ASID restores its JTC; a new ASID starts
    with an empty JTC. A change of FAST's table, a new MMUCR.SV, an AT
    edge and the engine choice drop every copy. OFF: a new ASID drops the
    translated slots, as before.

    fill takes the way of the same pc, else a stale way, else way 0 moves
    to way 1. An exception's vector is looked up through the cache too
    (`jmmu_exc_stub` goes to `loop_mmu_bc`).
  - With MMU Model FAST, a JTC miss, a block's first fetch and the JIT's
    pref find a page of FAST's table with no setjmp (`fast_try`); a page
    not in the table and every other case take the setjmp path as before.

  at SPEED ~35% (~11 fps), per second: 1.0M block lookups in C, ~425K
  store queue writes through C, ~38K TLB misses (Windows CE refills its

- Rows (SH4 / SYSTEM page, after SH4 MMU Engine; set before boot; the
  first value is the old path; default ON since HW run 1; in `[syscfg]`):
  - MMU Model FULL / FAST (`MmuFast`): Flycast's FAST_MMU (Flycast's
    default). Each entry that ldtlb loads stays in a table (32768 entries,
    8192 buckets) until MMUCR.TI or a TLB array write; a TLB array write
    leaves the table with what the UTLB holds after it. No ITLB, no
    protection, first-write or multi-hit checks, no URC count per access.
    An ldtlb of the same page, size and ASID (or both shared) with a new
    frame is a remap. Both engines.
  - MMU Block Cache OFF / ON (`MmuBlockCache`): the main loop looks up the
    next block in a 4096-entry table in PPC code (`emit_jmmu_dispatch`:
    pc, key = SR.MD, FPSCR PR, SZ, RM 1 and PTEH.ASID, generation, code)
    before the C lookup, which fills it. The generation moves at each
    change of a translation (a FAST remap or flush, MMUCR.SV), an I-cache
    flush, an AT edge and a code cache clear. With AT on it fills only
    with MMU Model FAST.
  - MMU SQ Stores C / INLINE (`MmuSqStores`): a JTC miss of a 32-bit or
    pair store into the store queues (the area bits, 4 or 8-byte aligned,
    in user mode only with MMUCR.SQMD 0) is written by the block; any
    other store goes to C as before.

  after 16 with an MMU engine (`dc/mem/mmu.cpp`); MMUCR writes in FAST
  drop the JTC only for TI or a new SV.

(Matt: "Keep it as up by default."), not packaged. Commit 0be5997 (Matt). `.got`

- Row SH4 MMU Engine (`MmuJit`, INTERP / JIT; SH4 / SYSTEM page, after
  SH4 MMU; default JIT in source since 2026-10-14 (Matt: "Yes."), INTERP
  before; set before boot; in `[syscfg]`).
  JIT: the boot that SH4 MMU picks (AUTO: a Windows CE disc) runs on the
  JIT with MMU blocks; any other boot gets the blocks of today. With the
  interpreter as the menu's engine the MMU interpreter runs, as before.
- Design (my choices, after Flycast's rec-x64 and rec-arm64 and the gate
  of P38 in section 7):
  - Blocks keyed by (virtual pc, physical pc, mode: SR.MD, FPSCR PR and
    SZ, RM 1), so one pc can have a block per frame (Windows CE maps each
    program at 0x00010000). Every block end goes to an MMU lookup in C
    (`jmmu_lookup`: the fetch through the ITLB with a 64-entry check cache,
    then the block); static links only inside the block's own 1 KB page.
  - Data accesses with AT on: an inline lookup in a 1 KB-page cache, the
    JTC (4 tables of 1024 entries, by mode and read/write), about 10 PPC
    words, that gives the host page. A miss calls the MMU interpreter's
    TLB path (UTLB, protection, exceptions, URC) and fills the JTC.
    ldtlb drops the slots of its entry and steps URC; a PTEH write with a
    new ASID, any MMUCR write and the TLB arrays drop every translated
    slot; an AT edge clears the code cache and the JTC.
  - Exceptions: a slow path leaves the code; the block's cold exit
    flushes the pinned GPRs and takes it (SPC = the op, or the branch of
    a delay slot); ops the JIT leaves to the interpreter run on the MMU
    interpreter's table (setjmp-wrapped; the PPU disassembly shows the
    wrapper saves r14-r31, f14-f31 and CR).
  - FPU disabled: a block with an FPU op tests SR.FD at its start (0x800
    with SPC = the block's start, as Flycast); SR.FD set when a block with
    an FPU op would compile raises it first, so FPSCR is right.
  - Code changes: no code cache clear on CCR.ICI (Windows CE flushes the
    I-cache 12-74 times a second). An I-cache flush moves an epoch; each
    1 KB code page is hashed again at its next lookup, and a changed page
    makes its blocks stale.
  - Off for AT 1 blocks: fastmem, SQ shapes, guard reuse, DYN_IC, BCACHE;
    off for the whole MMU boot: constprop, DVE (an exception between two
    ops must find every register written), the idle hash, the JIT_SBP
    guard. JIT RM 2/3 is ACCEPT for the boot. mac.l and mac.w, rte, pref
    and a branch whose delay slot is in the next page run on the MMU
    interpreter. Blocks end at a 1 KB page and at 96 ops; @-Rn stores
    move Rn after the write (as Flycast with the MMU).
- Logs: `[fullmmu] SH4 MMU AUTO, Windows CE disc yes: the MMU JIT runs
  this boot`, `[fullmmu] MMU JIT: blocks by (vaddr, paddr, mode) ...`,
  `[jitcfg] ... rmany=1`, the `[fullmmu] AT=1 | TLB miss ...` stats line,

registered a third area 0 handler; `_vmem` keeps a handler id * 4 in the

the tree now (7 of 7). The self-test line of that run was as expected (12
of 19461 failed with the rows OLD, the integer group clean).

- SOUND STOP in both HW runs (Matt, 2026-10-14: "At some point the
  audio goes COMPLETELY silent. Right at the end."). Cause found, NOT
  from this session's changes. Fix BUILT 2026-10-14 (Matt: "Yes,
  thanks."), package of 02:41, not committed. HW SUCCESS the same
  night (HW run 3, the last sub-bullet).
  - The log: `[arm7spe] no progress for 100 ms: SPU tail N-5 of N,
    exit 0x8001000F/0; ARM7 and AICA stop (no sound)` at line 8944
    (run 1) and 28589 (run 2, a second boot from line 13358, same
    file). It is the guard of `wait_tail()` in `ps3/ps3_arm_spe.cpp`:
    after it the PPU sends no more commands, so the sound is off for
    the rest of the boot. No older log of any session has this line.
  - The ARM7 SPU did not hang: the next `[arm7spe]` line has `lag 0`
    (it finished its queue), `timeouts 0`, `log waits 0`. The SH4
    thread did not wait 100 ms: in those seconds the stall probe has
    no frame over 20 ms and no section over 2.2 ms. So the timer of
    the guard was wrong, not the SPU.
  - Cause: `gettime()` (`ps3/include/ps3_timebase.h`, new at the
    cleanup of 2026-10-06) is a bare `mftb`. On the Cell a read at the
    moment the low 32 bits of the timebase roll over (each 2^32 /
    79.8 MHz = 53.82 s) can return the low half as 0 with the old high
    half: a time 53.8 s in the past. PSL1GHT's own `__gettime()`
    (`ppu/include/ppu-asm.h`) reads again while the low word is 0;
    ours does not. `wait_tail()` spins on `gettime()` (a read each 25
    ns) while the SH4 waits for the ARM7 SPU, 17-20% of the time in
    Sonic Adventure 2. One bad read makes `now - moved` a huge
    unsigned number, over the 100 ms limit.
  - Check on the log: the two stops are 1561 s apart (+- 1.3 s; the
    boot lines `time()=1791935467` and `1791936892`, the `[hb]`
    seconds). 29 rollovers are 1560.8 s.
  - Every other wait that spins on `gettime()` has the same risk (157
    uses of `gettime()` in ps3, dc and plugs): the fence waits of the
    render SPUs, `snd_answer()` of the PPU twin, the audio pacing.
  - Fix, built: the retry of PSL1GHT in `gettime()` (read again while
    the low 32 bits are 0), one header, no row. In the ELF 242 of the
    261 `mftb` reads have the retry (a compare of the low word with
    0 and a branch back), the two reads of `wait_tail()` with them.
    The PC checks have their own stub of the header, so no check
    runs this code: the proof is an HW run. HW test: Sonic Adventure
    2 for 10 minutes or more (11 rollovers) with no `no progress for
    100 ms` line and no silence.
  - Not changed: the guard still ends the sound for good when it
    fires. The other 19 reads are the TA split probe
    (`ps3/ps3_tasplit.h`, its own bare `mftb`): a wrong stamp there
    is a wrong sample of a log line, not a stop.
  - HW run 3, 2026-10-14 02:42 (Matt, Sonic Adventure 2, the boot at
    log line 30678, stamp `Oct 14 2026 00:40:13`): "The audio didn't
    cut off this time and (despite the slowdowns) it sounded fine!

    correctly." The log: 428 s, 7 or 8 rollovers, no `no progress`

  - CAUSE FOUND (code + this census + a PC estimate), NOT BUILT: the
    wrap of an ADPCM stream. The scene's sound is the stereo stream
    above: PCMS 3, LSA 0, LEA 8191, a ring of 8192 nibbles per side
    (the two rings are 0x1000 bytes apart). In `stream_step()` and
    `slot_fast()` (`plugs/caiqueAICA/aica_model.cpp:476-485`,
    `:1506-1514`) a stream tests the loop end on `CA & ~3`, so the
    test fires at CA 8192, and `CA -= LEA - LSA` then gives 1. Ring
    position 0 is not decoded on any lap after the first: one ADPCM
    nibble of the stream is lost per lap, 2.7 times per second on
    each side. ADPCM is a delta format with a step state, so each
    lost nibble shifts the level and the offset of that side for the
    rest of the stream, and the two sides shift apart.
  - Flycast wraps to LSA (`sgc_if.cpp`, `alignedLEA`): no nibble is
    lost. The caique console case (`cases/sgc_formats.c`) loops over
    [0, 4096): its LEA is a multiple of 4, and for such a LEA the two
    rules are equal. So the console data does not cover LEA 8191,
    and a ring of 8192 nibbles with LEA 8191 decodes as one stream
    only with Flycast's rule. This is 6.9 B's item "ADPCM long
    stream (PCMS 3) with LEA & 3 != 0", which had no game.

**Flycast sound review 2026-10-13 (Matt: "check on Flycast's audio
driver, and see what differs from ours", for the faults of bundle 18;
then he asked for the findings in this file). Read-only: nothing is
built, no HW run, no row changed. 130 review agents: 12 readers by
subsystem and by fault, then 6 more for the gaps that a critic named.
They reported 111 differences. A skeptic checked each one against the
code of both trees, the row defaults, the byte order and the HW logs of
bundle 18: none was refuted, 96 were corrected in part. The text is 6.9
(parts A to H). Short form, per fault:**
- Loud effects (Sonic Adventure 2, Spider-Man): no cause in the sound
  code. Both sides clamp the mix once at 16 bits with the same gain. One
  voice of ours is -0.07 to +0.93 dB against Flycast at MVOL 15, +1.45
  dB on the far side of an odd pan step, +1.96 dB with an odd MVOL too
  (P81). The peaks of 120-275% need 1.6 to 8.8 dB on the whole mix. The
  loud part is the dry mix: run 2 had no DSP, and Spider-Man has no
  reverb at all with DSP Ring 64K OFF. Open: the registers the game
  writes and the voice count (lead 2 of bundle 18), and 6.7. (6.9 A)
- Crackle: two sources, neither shown to be the reported one.
  - ADPCM loops with a loop start above 0. Ours (default path) restarts
    the decoder at each lap. Flycast and nullAICA restore the state
    saved at the loop start. The console rule is not measured. Sonic
    Adventure 2 uses such loops: 6 of the 8 decoded loops of run 4 play
    8-27 dB lower from lap 2. No HW run tested the rule. Candidate: a
    row "ADPCM Loop" RESET / RESTORE, about 30 lines. (6.9 B)
  - Silent output blocks of 5.3 ms when SPEED is under 100%: in about
    40 of 180 seconds of run 1. Run 2 has none in the stage and the
    fault stayed, so this is a second crackle, not the reported one.
    (6.9 F)
- Music restart (Sonic Adventure 2): no difference in the stream path.
  The stage file `C_ESCAP1.ADX` (16 kHz mono in this image) loops by
  itself at 129.8 s, back to sample 0. No log shows a restart without
  a START press. Only run 1 plays past 129.8 s. Open: what Flycast
  plays at 129.8 s (PC, no build). (6.9 C)
- Key-off at 2 s (Sonic Adventure 2): not a fault. It is 119 video
  frames, set on the game side, and the slot is already silent. Lead 3
  of bundle 18 is closed for this game. (6.9 D)
- SH4 wait for the sound SPUs (Sonic Adventure 2): cause found. At +
  SAMPLE SYNC a G2 DMA write near a play point syncs with no test
  (likely the music feed; the target is not logged): 75-77 syncs/s,
  13.9-14.5% of wall. The long part is the DSP: 1250-1405 us per sync,
  against 45 us with SPE AICA DSP OFF (3.6% of wall). A cost for bundle
  22, not a sound fault. Candidate: 6.6 step (a), a range test per G2
  DMA. (6.9 F)
- Looney Tunes balance: not explained. Its DSP program is empty on ours
  ("113 words, 2 live steps" is the floor of a program that stores
  nothing), so "the voices go through the DSP only" does not hold. The
  AUDIO64 driver (Looney Tunes, Spider-Man, Ecco the Dolphin) writes a
  key-off and a key-on 379-388 ticks apart. About 73% of the pairs
  fall in one ARM7 run, and a slot that is not in release then drops
  the start. A lead for missing effects: no log has it, and Matt's
  "The sound cues ALL played correctly" (2026-10-07) is against it.
  (6.9 D, E)
- Baseline: Flycast's DSP is OFF by default, and no state of row "SPE
  AICA DSP" gives that mix. An ear test against Flycast needs its
  "Enable DSP" ON (P81 step 2, never run). (6.9 E)
- Do not port (ours follows the console, Flycast does not): the
  one-shot end, rate 0 with key rate scaling, the ALFO depth, the
  filter bypass, the loop-end partner, the 20-bit DSP bus wrap, the key
  at the KYONEX write, Flycast's DSP rules, 512 ARM7 ticks as a default.
- Checks with no build, recommended order:
  1. PC: Flycast, the same .cdi, City Escape for 2 min 10 s with no
     pause, death or Restart: does the song jump at 129.8 s?
  2. PC: Flycast with "Enable DSP" OFF then ON: Looney Tunes (a menu
     voice line and a race) and one Sonic Adventure 2 stage.
  3. HW: Sonic Adventure 2, the stage of the runs, row "SPE AICA Gain"
     at 80%, 50%, then cfg key `SpeAicaGain=35`. Read `clip/s`, `peak`
     and `[aud] silent=`. Distortion at `clip/s=0/0` and `silent=0`
     means the clamp is not the cause.
  4. HW: Looney Tunes and Spider-Man, row "ARM7 Interleave" SLICE
     against SAMPLE, live: listen for missing or cut effects.
     Spider-Man with DSP Ring 64K OFF, then ON.
- Candidate changes, none built, Matt picks: the row "ADPCM Loop"; the
  G2 DMA range test (6.6 step (a)); the RING interval fix (about 10
  lines, before DSP Ring 64K can be a default); the key pass at a
  second KYONEX write (15-20 lines, a row); the G2 DMA register masks

- Data: `result.json` (the 111 differences with their checks),

  Package of 16:56. HW SUCCESS in run 4 (below).**
  - What it is: the vertices of a polygon with an offset colour take the
    builder's fast step (`strip_fast()`, two vertices at a time), each
    with its colour from the array beside the vertices (one load and
    one shuffle more per vertex, `uv_offs()`). The exact step stays for
    the vertices that the fast step leaves, as for a plain polygon. The
    step is in each pass, as the plain one (not a call per strip). The
    in-order pass takes the offset window inside that step, so a plain
    strip no longer tests its param for it.
  - The SPU simulator (`misc/spevb_check/sim.sh`, the real image, new
    option `OFFS=percent` of the params with the Offset bit; a scene of
    38400 vertices, time per build):

    | Scene | Exact step (package of 14:10) | Fast step (package of 16:56) |
    |---|---|---|
    | No offset colour | 2.29 ms | 2.25 ms |
    | 60% of the vertices with one | 6.53 ms | 2.41 ms |
    | Each vertex with one | 9.15 ms | 2.50 ms |

    The exact step's 4.0 times agrees with HW run 2 (3.7 to 3.9 times).
    A scene of 15000 vertices: 0.89 ms plain (HW run of bundle 14: 936
    us), 0.99 ms with a colour on each vertex (HW run 2: 3670 us). So
    the estimate for Sonic Adventure is about 1.0 ms, not measured on

    takes with no hint, and the colour's load.

- The rows (`[rendcfg]` line at boot and at a menu change; cfg keys
  PtBlend, SpriteCorner, OffsetColour, ColourClamp, Trilinear; all act

  | Row | Values (first = old path) | What it does |
  |---|---|---|
  | PT Blend | OFF / ON / + ALPHA 1 | + ALPHA 1: a punch-through texel that passes the alpha test has alpha 1 (Flycast's GL renderer). SRC_ALPHA acts as ONE and INV_SRC_ALPHA as ZERO; a polygon that then has ONE and ZERO draws with no blend (the punch-through list of Jet Grind Radio). ON is the default since bundle 4. |
  | Sprite Corner | OLD / PLANE | PLANE: a sprite's fourth corner takes its 1/W, u and v from the plane through the other three, at its own x and y. OLD: A + C - B, right only for a parallelogram. A parallelogram keeps the old corner, bit for bit. Acts at the next list init. |
  | Offset Colour | OFF / ON | ON: a textured polygon with the Offset bit adds its offset colour after the texture (highlights on models). The two decoders keep one offset colour per vertex; the draw sends it with each vertex of such a polygon. Acts at the next list init. |
  | Colour Clamp | OFF / ON | ON: a polygon with the ColorClamp bit clamps its colour to FOG_CLAMP_MIN..FOG_CLAMP_MAX before the fog. As Flycast, it acts only when the registers clamp something (MIN not 00000000 or MAX not FFFFFFFF). |
  | Trilinear | OFF / ON | ON: the two passes of a trilinear polygon (FilterMode 2 and 3, a mipmapped texture, not the punch-through list) draw with the weights 1 - f and f; f is a quarter of MipMapD's low 2 bits. OFF: both passes at full weight (too bright). |

- Traps:
  - Offset Colour ON has a cost: 4 more bytes per vertex from the SPU
    decoder (+1 to 2 points of its busy in HW run 2), and one more load
    per vertex in the SPU builder (the simulator: about 10% more build
    time; HW run 2 had the exact step: 3.8 times). Read `[spevb] spu
    busy` and `[rend] busy` against a boot with the row OFF.
  - Offset Colour and Sprite Corner are decode options: the lists of the
    frame in progress keep the old value.
  - With Offset Colour ON a scene with vertex fog (Fog at + VERTEX)
    stays on the SPU path, because its lists hold the offset colours. A
    bump scene (Rayman 2) still goes to the PPU replay.
  - Colour Clamp and Trilinear draw with programs that read three new
    texture coordinates (2, 3, 4) from a new vertex program. That form
    has no HW run. The Offset Colour programs use only the forms of the
    bump and the fog programs, which are HW proven.
  - Trilinear makes a polygon darker when a game draws only one of the
    two passes with a MipMapD that is not a whole number. Flycast does
    the same.
  - With Render Thread OFF the PPU replay runs with the game's rounding
    mode. A trapezoid sprite can then differ from the SPU's by one bit,
    and the S2 compare says so.
- New log lines, with every row OFF too:
  - `[rend17] pt_blend= corner= offs= clamp= tril= | opt= lists_offs=
    planes ppu= spu= | applied offs= clamp= tril= | fog_clamp min= max=`
    each 5 s. `planes`: sprites that took the plane's corner (the PPU
    replay, the SPU decoder). `applied`: states drawn with the offset
    colour program, with the clamp, with a weight under 1. `fog_clamp`:
    the last render's registers; a game can use Colour Clamp only when
    min is not 00000000 or max is not FFFFFFFF.
  - A fourth `[rendz]` line per list: `offs= cclamp= tril=a/b pt_one=
    spr_quad=` = the last render's strips with an offset colour, with
    the ColorClamp bit, trilinear passes with a weight under 1 / all
    trilinear passes, punch-through strips that + ALPHA 1 draws with no
    blend, sprites whose fourth corner is not the parallelogram's. So
    one boot with the rows OFF tells which rows a game can use.
- The code:
  - `ps3/spu/spe_sprite.h` (new): the plane, one text for the PPU replay
    and the SPU decoder. Doubles in single steps (each product goes
    through memory, so no compiler fuses it with an add), Cramer's rule,
    a value outside 2^-40..2^40 keeps the old corner. The SPU has no
    exact double divide (its libgcc call is a Newton step), so it takes
    the quotient bit by bit.
  - `ps3/spu/spe_bell.h`: TAOPT_SPR_PLANE (32), TAOPT_OFFS (64),
    `SpeOut.offs` (one word per vertex; 1 MB more main memory for the
    four contexts), `SpeEcho.spr_plane`.
  - `ps3/spu/spe_dec.c`: a sixth output stream (the offset colours), the
    face offset colour of PolyParam 2B, the sprite's corner.
  - `ps3/spu/spe_vb_build.h` (flag SPEVB_OFFS): input windows for the
    offset colours in the in-order passes, the sorted TR ring and long
    strips; `strip_fast()` with its constant `offs` (`uv_offs()`),
    `strip_rest_offs()`. The 24-byte vertex did not change, and a plain
    polygon's fast step is the same code as before.
  - `ps3/ps3_rend.cpp`: the decoder (`VTX_NO_OFFS`, the sprite),
    `offc_param()` and `run_offs()`, `xt_apply()`, `tril_weight()`, the
    punch-through factors in `apply_param_body()`, the two log lines.
    `draw_modvols()` turns the new programs off: the volumes have no
    texture and would take the last polygon's clamp.
  - ps3gl: 39 fragment programs and one vertex program
    (`shaders/dc_fp.fcg`, `dc_vp.vcg`, `compile_dc.sh`,
    `ps3gl_shader_dc.h`; the older shader headers are not touched),
    `ps3gl_dc_offs()`, `ps3gl_dc_xt()`, the table `dc_tab`.
  - Sizes: the decoder's SPU image 128264 bytes of 262144; the builder's
    248768 with the fast step (13.3 KB left for its stack; 20 KB in the
    package of 14:10, 30 KB before the bundle); `.got` 0xECB8 of 0x10000
    (4.8 KB left).
- My choices, not Matt's words:

- Traps:
  - VMU Per Game: the file of a game starts blank. The old saves stay
    in `vmu_save_A1.bin` and come back when the row is OFF; nothing is
    copied and nothing is deleted. A boot with no disc uses the shared
    files. A disc swap keeps the card of the boot disc. The ID is the
    product number of IP.BIN (10 bytes at 0x40), so two discs with the
    same number share a file.
  - Maple Bus Speed REAL makes each DMA longer: a block read is 5.8 ms
    of emulated time (2.0 ms at OLD), a pad poll 0.25 ms (0.09 ms). The
    end of a DMA is tested each 28672 SH4 cycles (0.14 ms) at Accuracy
    FAST, at both values.
  - The VMU screen is black dots on white, opaque (as the FPS box), and
    turned 180 degrees, as Flycast shows it.
- New log lines, with every row OFF too: `[vmu] disc ID 'MK-51000', VMU
  Per Game 0` at each boot with a disc, and `[vmu] A1: first LCD
  picture` at the first LCD write of a slot. So each boot tells the
  disc's ID and if the game uses the VMU screen.
- Facts from the old logs (8.2 GB of scratchpad text; the search was cut

  18).
- The code:
  - `dc/maple/maple_if.cpp`: a pool of reply words (8192 words, 128
    replies; when it is full the kept replies are written early, with a
    `[maple] reply pool full` line). A reply is built in the pool when a
    row changes it; with every row OFF the device writes into RAM as
    before. `maple_Update()` copies the replies, raises the overrun
    interrupt, then the end interrupt.
  - Byte order: the pool, the swapped frame and the replies are native
    u32 words; the devices write them with their XOR-3 byte view, and
    the SB_MMSEL swap is on the u32 values (P29, P68).
  - `plugins/plugin_header.h`: `holly_MAPLE_OVERRUN` (error bit 9).
  - `dc/maple/maple_devs.cpp`: the commands of the pad and the VMU;
    the VMU's file by `vmu_file_name()` (`maple_vmu_name.h`) and
    `maple_vmu_game()`, which `apply_disc_meta()` (`dc/dc.cpp`) calls
    with the disc's product number.
  - `ps3/ps3_vmulcd.cpp`: the VMU screens, which `maple_cfg.cpp` feeds
    and `frame_extras()` (`ps3/ps3_rend.cpp`) draws after the FPS text.
  - `.got` is 0xEBF8 of 0x10000 (5.0 KB left).
- My choices, not Matt's words:
  - One row per fault, not one per P number: the two guards share a
    row, and SB_MMSEL shares a row with the recipient address (one
    Flycast commit).
  - Maple VBlank DMA FIXED is Flycast's rule (SB_MDST stays set to the
    end), not Reicast's (set, then cleared at once).
  - VMU Per Game has a level ALL SLOTS; Flycast has only slot A1.
  - Not taken from Flycast 8192eea38: "a device with no expansion
    ports takes every frame of its bus". P68 names only the two rules
    that are built.
  - Not built: the VMU beep (bundle 18), a copy of the old saves into
    a new per-game file, a position row for the VMU screen.

  | Console ID | OLD / FLYCAST | FLYCAST: a blank console ID (0x1a058) gets a random one in both copies; the checksum is set; the machine version is 0xFE. |
  | Exit Flash Save | OFF / ON | The forced exit (3 s after an XMB quit that the SH4 does not answer) saves the flash first. Live. |
  | RTC Local Time | OFF / ON | The Dreamcast clock is UTC + the XMB's time zone + its summer time. OFF: UTC, as it is today. |

- Facts from the old logs (the scratchpads of the older sessions):
  - The clock: in each of 293 old boots (2026-10-03 to 2026-10-13) the
    `[nullDC] RTC=` line is `time()` + 631152000 with no offset. So the
    PS3's `time()` is UTC, its C library has no time zone, and
    `tm_isdst` is 0. The Dreamcast clock is UTC: 2 hours behind in the
    Italian summer, 1 hour in the winter. P12's line (one day, not one
    hour, under summer time) is fixed, but that line never runs on the
    PS3. It needs no row.
  - The broadcast byte: every boot starts at `PAL480i50.00` (the BIOS),
    so the flash holds a PAL byte. The byte itself was never printed:
    the new `[flash]` line of HW run 1 shows it.
  - 10 of the 23 games of the old logs stay at 50 Hz in every boot, not
    3 as P59 says: Rayman 2 (8 boots), Soul Calibur (6), Space Channel 5
    (4), Border Down (3), Capcom vs. SNK 2 (3), Ikaruga (3), Sonic
    Shuffle (3), Spider-Man (3), Sega Rally 2 (2), Shenmue (2). Power
    Stone 2 is at 50 Hz in 3 of 5 boots, Rez in 2 of 3. Crazy Taxi,
    Sonic Adventure, Sonic Adventure 2, Looney Tunes, ChuChu Rocket,
    Quake III Arena, Phantasy Star Online, Jet Grind Radio and Ecco the
    Dolphin switch to NTSC by themselves (a boot counts once: the logs
    are split per `[menu] launching` line and per RTC value).
  - Each disc image of the old logs lists the area `JUE`, and the flash
    region is 1 (USA). So for Matt's discs DISC gives what NTSC gives.
  - The BIOS settings block is in physical block 224 to 241 of the 254
    of the user partition, a new one at each BIOS save. For GOALS.md
    G11: the dial-up blocks 0x80-0xEA need about 107 free blocks, and
    Flycast's `alloc_block` takes a block again when a newer copy of its
    data exists. Ours has no such rule (not built here: it changes the
    old path for a flash with no settings block).
- The code:
  - `dc/flash_fix.cpp` (header `dc/flash_fix.h`): `dc_flash_build()`
    (Flycast's `Validate()` on an empty chip, then its Region 1,
    Language 1 and Broadcast 0), `dc_flash_set_time()` (as before, with
    the language of a new block and the row's language),
    `dc_flash_fixup()` (the rows' factory bytes, the console ID),
    `dc_flash_set_region()` (as before, with the DISC rule),
    `dc_flash_report()` and `dc_flash_restore_region()`.
    `LoadBiosFiles()` (`dc/dc.cpp`) calls them in that order.
  - The `[flash]` line, new, at each boot with every row OFF too:
    `[flash] region=R language=L broadcast=B (flash file: R L B) syscfg
    language=N (flash file: N) console id=XXXXXXXXXXXX checksum=ok|bad
    version=XX user blocks=N/254`. The first values are what the BIOS
    and the game read. The values after "flash file" are the file's own.
  - `dc/mem/sh4_mem.cpp`: `mem_SaveFlashForced()` for the monitor
    thread (`ps3/ps3_main.cpp`). It saves only a flash that
    `LoadBiosFiles()` marked as loaded (`g_flash_loaded`), and one lock
    lets one thread write the file at a time. Log: `[flash] forced exit:
    flash saved`.
  - `dc/aica/aica_if.cpp` `GetRTC_now()` and `ps3/ps3_main.cpp`
    `ps3_local_offset_seconds()`
    (`sysUtilGetSystemParamInt(SYSUTIL_SYSTEMPARAM_ID_TIMEZONE)` and
    `..._SUMMERTIME`). Log at each boot, with the row OFF too: `[rtc]
    PS3 time zone N min (rc X), summer time N (rc X)`.
  - `nullDC.cpp`: a missing `dc_flash.bin` ends the boot only at Flash
    Defaults OLD.
  - Byte order: none. `misc/flash_check/run.sh` fails if
    `dc/flash_fix.cpp` holds a `(u16*)` or a `(u32*)` cast.
- My choices, not in the plan text and not Matt's words:
  - Row RTC Local Time. P12's one line cannot make the clock right on
    the PS3 (the fact above), so the row takes the offset from the XMB.
    The unit of the summer-time value is not verified (minutes are
    assumed; a value of 1 counts as 60). The `[rtc]` line of HW run 1
    shows the two raw values before the row is ON.
  - No row's value reaches `dc_flash_wb.bin`, but the console ID: the
    factory bytes and the settings block's language go back to the
    flash's own before each save, as the region did. A language that
    the user picks in the BIOS in the same run stays. So a row acts
    again at each boot, and CONSOLE gives back the flash's own value.
  - Flash Defaults holds two items of P85 in one row: the built flash
    and the English default of a new settings block. Flycast's
    `Validate()` runs only when no file loads: a flash that loads is
    not repaired, and its partition 1 is not erased (Flycast erases it
    at each boot).
  - The new console ID comes from an own generator with the RTC as
    seed, not from `rand()`.
  - Exit Flash Save is a row and is live, with the lock and the
    "loaded" flag: a forced exit before the flash loads must not write
    an empty flash over the saved one.
  - Not taken: Flycast's PAL-M and PAL-N values and its per-game
    broadcast lists (a list per game); the `SaveSettings()` call at an
    RTC write (P85's "Also" line, no effect).

- The DRAW COST page (page 12 of 12; a `[costcfg]` line at boot and at a
  menu change; all three rows are live):
  - (The first value of each row is the old path; the defaults are ON
    since the verdict.)
  - Tex Bind Table (`TexBindTable`): OFF / ON. ps3gl finds the slot of a
    texture name in a table of 4096 entries, indexed by the name's low
    bits. An entry holds the slot of the last texture with those bits; a
    hit must still hold the name, a miss takes the old scan. OFF scans up
    to 4096 slots at each bind (the 11.1 points of HW run 5 of 3k).
  - GL State Compare (`GlCompare`): OFF / ON. ON:
    - A state setter (blend, alpha, depth, cull, scissor, viewport, colour
      mask, polygon offset, shade model, stencil) marks its group only
      when a value changes. OFF marks it at each call, and the next draw
      sends the whole group again.
    - A texture parameter that keeps its value does not mark the texture.
      OFF marks it at each call: the 5 parameters of each bind send 4 RSX
      calls at the next draw.
    - At a texture change, the unit's control, filter and wrap words go
      out only when they differ from the words the unit holds. The
      texture itself always goes out.
    - The 4 vertex attribute binds stay when the next draw has the same
      block, stride, colour shift and texcoord1 form. So in a scene they
      go out at the first draw, and again when a bump or fog program (the
      texcoord1 form) or the colour shift comes or goes.
  - TR First Pass (`TrFirstPass`): OLD / SKIP / + GAME ORDER. It acts on
    the first pass of TR Triangle Sort + OPAQUE DEPTH only.
    - SKIP (Flycast's depth pass): a run that writes no depth (its blend
      hides nothing, or the polygon has ZWriteDis) is not applied and not
      drawn. OLD applies each run, and draws a ZWriteDis run with every
      mask off.
    - + GAME ORDER: the first pass goes out before the sort, in submission
      order, so its runs are as long as the merged strips. The depth it
      leaves does not depend on the draw order. It writes its own corners
      (only the runs it draws); when the scene's vertex block is too short
      for them, the rest of the scene goes to a second block.
- Counters only, as the bundle says (no row, no change of the draws):
  - The merge key: `[cost] key op=A>B pt=A>B tr=A>B`. A = state changes
    from strip to strip by the merge key of today; B = by the bits a draw
    reads. A - B is the draws a mask on the key can save. It is the last
    render of each 5 s window, in submission order.
  - The texture lifetime: `[texlife] aged=N back=N same=N` per window.
    aged = textures freed after 180 frames with no draw; back = cache
    misses whose key one of them had; same = of those, the ones with the
    same texels (a decode that Flycast's rule saves).

- The cause is confirmed with the PS3 compiler
  (`misc/mmu_check/bitfield_ppu.sh`, the build image's ppu-g++ at -O2):
  the MMUCR bitfield reads AT from bit 4, TI from bit 6, SV from bit 12,
  SQMD from bit 13, URC from bits 19-14 and URB from bits 25-20. Only LRUI
  is at its bits. So the emulator never sees a game turn the MMU on.
- A new MEMORY page (page 11 of 11; a `[memcfg]` line at boot and at a
  menu change):
  - MMUCR Bits: OLD / FIXED (set before boot). FIXED:
    - The fields come from masks on the register word, at the manual's
      bits (AT 0, TI 2, URC 15-10, URB 23-18). The readers are the MMUCR
      write, `ldtlb`, the interpreters' PREF and the JIT (PREF target,
      JIT PREFETCH, JIT GUARD REUSE). OLD reads the bitfield as before.
    - A write keeps the real bits only (0xFCFCFF05, Flycast).
    - An AT change clears the JIT code cache, on both edges (Flycast): the
      JIT reads AT when it compiles a block.
    - TI clears the V bit of each TLB entry and keeps the store-queue
      remap table (Flycast's `mmu_flush_table`). OLD clears the table too.
      The reason: no TLB miss comes to the emulator, so nothing loads a
      cleared slot again. P58's text counted "the table is not cleared" as
      a fault; that part is not taken.
    - A UTLB entry in the store-queue area with V = 0 leaves its remap
      slot as it is (Flycast's `UTLB_Sync` without FAST_MMU).
    - A UTLB or ITLB data-array write with address bit 23 goes to the
      assistance word (data array 2), not into PPN and V (Flycast,
      Reicast). The reads are as before (Flycast returns data array 1).
  - P4 Mirrors: OFF / ON (set before boot). ON maps VRAM at 0xE4-0xE7 and
    main RAM at 0xEC-0xEF, after the P4 handler (Flycast 156aafe95). OFF:
    those pages read 0 and drop writes, as before. The other pages of
    Flycast's mirror hold nothing in our map (areas 2, 4, 5, 6).
  - Cache RAM Banks: OLD / FLYCAST (set before boot). FLYCAST: the on-chip
    RAM is two 4 KB banks; the bank is address bit 13, or bit 25 when
    CCR.OIX is set. OLD takes the low 13 address bits, so 0x7C000000 and
    0x7C002000 are the same bytes (on the SH4 they are bank 1 and bank 2).
  - Ch2 DMA Rules: OLD / FLYCAST (live). FLYCAST:
    - The target is (SB_C2DSTAT & 0x03FFFFE0) | 0x10000000 and the length
      is SB_C2DLEN & 0x00FFFFE0, applied when the DMA starts (Flycast
      masks at the register write; the registers' read-back is not
      changed here).
    - Nothing is refused: an odd length is cut, a zero length ends at
      once, both with TE and the end interrupt. OLD returns with no
      interrupt and SB_C2DST still 1.
    - 0x12xxxxxx is the TA's mirror (polygons and YUV). OLD moves no data
      there.
    - A DMAOR write keeps bits 15, 9, 8 and 2-0 (0x8307). This also
      helps the PVR and GD-ROM DMAs, which test the same register.
- Bundle 1's rows for these games stay on VIDEO / DEBUG, with no code
  change: LMMODE (test: Rez), FB Write Watch (test: Ikaruga), VRAM Direct.
- Not built: the flat store-queue flush for AT = 1 (P74). The plan takes

  RAM SQ Direct do not act for these games.

    fb_alpha_threshold, channels rounded, each pixel at its clip
    position, the row cut at FB_W_LINESTRIDE, no copy in pack modes 4-7,
    the target cleared to alpha 0.

    for a free buffer; a 2D present that found none is tried again at the
    next vblank.

    acts at the next video mode write: set before boot.
  - Blank Video: OFF / ON (P76): a 2D present with VO_CONTROL bit 3 shows
    VO_BORDER_COL.
  - Present Rule: ALL / SHOWN / + KEEP COLOUR (P60). SHOWN: a render is
    flipped at its end only if FB_R_SOF1 holds its FB_W_SOF1; else it
    stays in the back buffer, and the game's FB_R_SOF1/2 write flips it
    (`FbShown()`, called from `plugs/drkPvr/regs.cpp`). + KEEP COLOUR: a
    render over a frame that waits does not clear the colour, unless its
    buffer is not one of the last two (Flycast's rule). With the rule on,
    a render to texture draws on its own RSX surface (3.7 MB of RSX
    memory, always allocated), not in the back buffer. Frame Hold places
    no flip for a frame that waits.
  - Region Scissor: OFF / ON (P60): a render draws only inside the region
    array's tiles and the FB clip (the clip times the scaler's factors).
  - Keep Last Frame: OFF / ON (P60, added in the package of 19:52): a
    render that Region Scissor cuts starts from a copy of the last flipped
    frame, not from black (the entry at the end of this block).
  - FB Reads: OLD / FLYCAST (P26): two interlaced fields one line apart
    are read as one image, else the shown field; 240 lines at the 13.5
    MHz clock; 24-bit frames are converted (on the PPU).

- What the row draws (Flycast `core/rend/dx9/d3d_shaders.cpp` pp_FogCtrl;
  Reicast `glesrend.cpp` is the same):
  - TABLE. FogCtrl 0: colour = lerp(colour, FOG_COL_RAM, table(FOG_DENSITY
    / W)), per pixel, after the texture. FogCtrl 3: (FOG_COL_RAM, table
    value) is the base colour before the texture. Bump polygons take the
    FogCtrl 0 fog too (Rayman 2's overlay).
  - + VERTEX. FogCtrl 1 with a texture, the Offset bit and no bump map:
    colour = lerp(colour, FOG_COL_VERT, offset alpha). Only the PPU replay
    keeps offset colours (3j's design A), so a scene with such a polygon
    decodes and builds on the PPU, as Rayman 2's bump scenes do
    (`[fog] ppu=`). That is why it is a level of its own.
  - Not built: the offset colour add (3b), the colour clamp
    (FOG_CLAMP_MIN/MAX), FogCtrl 3 on a bump polygon (it draws as before).
- How:
  - `RenderRegs` takes FOG_COL_RAM, FOG_COL_VERT, FOG_DENSITY and the 128
    table words at STARTRENDER, only with the row on. They are native u32.
  - One 512 x 4 linear texture on TMU 1 (`fog_upload()` in
    `ps3/ps3_rend.cpp`; written again only when a register changes). Rows
    0-1: FOG_COL_RAM and the table's value at z = 2^(8 (k + 0.5) / 512).
    Rows 2-3: FOG_COL_VERT. So the fragment program reads the table at
    s = saturate(-log2(W / density) / 8): one LG2, no floor, no pow, and
    no fragment constant to patch. The saturate is the PVR's z clamp.
  - `fog_vp.vcg` is `bump_vp` + texcoord0.z = position.z x fogp.x.
    position.z is W; fogp.x = 1 / FOG_DENSITY, a VP constant per scene.
    The RSX interpolates it with perspective: that is the PVR's 1/W per
    pixel. The SPU's vertices need no change.
  - 14 fragment programs from one source (`fog_fp.fcg`, `compile_fog.sh`,
    `ps3gl_shader_fog.h`; `ps3gl_shader_data.h` is not touched): table fog
    x (no texture, modulate, replace, decal, 3 bump), vertex fog x 3, base
    colour x 4. `ps3gl_dc_fog(mode)` picks the key (`ps3gl_shaders.c`
    `fog_key()`); `apply_param_body()` sets the mode per polygon.
  - New on hardware: LG2, a second texture unit, texcoord0 with 3
    components. The rest is what the bump programs use. The binaries were
    decoded (opcodes, units, masks, the `fogp` constant at c[4]).

- Why: HW run 23 (below). The game's vertex loop 8C141BBA is 22-26% of
  the JIT's hot instructions at 14K+ vertices, and each of its 5
  store-queue stores per vertex fails the RAM test and goes out of line
  (`coldin/s` 5.0 per turn). JIT SQ STORES wants a `pref` on the store's
  own register in the block; JIT SQ MISS's look-ahead wants it in the
  first 6 ops of a successor. This loop stores through r6 and does `pref
  @r3; mov r6,r3`.
- What: row JIT SPEED -> "JIT SQ COPY" (`JitSqCopy`), default OFF, set
  before boot. `sqcp_guess()` (`ps3/ps3_jit_sqla.h`): the block PREFs
  through Rm, and Rm's only writer in the block is `mov Rn,Rm` with Rn
  the store's base; no interpreter op and no SR sync in the block. It
  only picks the shape (store-queue test inline, RAM in the cold path):
  `emit_sq_check` still tests the address, so a wrong guess costs speed,
  not correctness. It needs JIT SQ STORES ON. Both guess sites take it
  (`gr_prepare` and the `shop_writem` case of `ps3/ps3_driver.cpp`).
- Log: `[jitcfg] sqcopy=`, `[ta-split] ... sqcp=<sites since boot>`.
  With JIT HOTBLOCKS: `coldin/s` of 8C141BBA must fall from 5 per turn
  to 0.

- JIT BCACHE (5.3): a dynamic block end (rts at the default DYN IC level,
  and each DYN IC miss) looks up `bm_bcache[]`, 8-byte {addr, code}
  entries: 9 instructions, two loads, no store (`ps3/ps3_jit_bcache.h`).
  The old path is about 16 with a `lookups++` load and store.
  `BlockCacheFlatEntry.code` is now a u32 (it was a pointer: 16 bytes on
  PPC64, so the path could not run). `loop_no_update` still calls
  `bm_GetCode` in C after a timeslice. Known side effect: a hit does not
  count `lookups`, so two hot blocks in one bucket can take turns in the
  cached slot (each turn is a few C lookups). Expected gain: noise level.
- JIT MAC fix (5.3): the S = 0 result is one 64-bit add of `extsw`,
  `extsw`, `mulld` on MACH:MACL (`ps3/ps3_jit_mac.h`, 7 instructions; every
  one is in the HW validated 5.2 and 5.38 forms). The old form took the
  carry of a 64-bit `addc`: on the PC model it is wrong in 26.2% of random
  mac.l cases, 6.2% of mac.w, and in 1 of Flycast's 4 mac cases (mac.w
  -21 + 35). The S = 1 call to `sh4_mac_l` / `sh4_mac_w` is not changed.
  **No game in any old `[IFB]` log runs mac.l or mac.w** (Crazy Taxi,
  Sonic Adventure, Soul Calibur, Rayman 2, ChuChu Rocket, Looney Tunes), so
  no HW test game is known: `[jit8] mac=` shows if a game compiles one.

    `[ni] NI=0: 1e-30*1e-10=000116C2 den*1=00000123 den+den=00000246 |
    ns/op: normal 5.4, den result 4.8, den operand 47.8`; `NI=1:` the same
    three values, `normal 4.7, den result 4.7, den operand 45.8`. So NI = 1
    flushes no denormal result and zeroes no denormal operand, and it
    saves no time. A denormal result costs nothing. A denormal operand
    costs about 10 times a normal op (about 43 ns more) with NI = 0 and
    with NI = 1; the probe loads the operand with `lfs` in each turn, so
    the cost can be the load (not split). FPU DN has no effect to test:
    HW step 5 falls away. **5.40 CLOSED by Matt 2026-10-11 ("Perfect. You

- Matt 2026-10-11: "Reicast has an Idle skill loop detection. How about we
  take that one?" Read (`libswirl/hw/sh4/dyna/decoder.cpp:30-63`,
  `:1147-1188`, `driver.cpp:171-207`; Minicast the same): (1) the x3 rule,
  which is our X3 BACKWARD; (2) `idle_hash`, a fixed list of 12 block
  hashes (4 BIOS, 3 "SC", 2 "HH", 3 more) that bill `max_cycles`, so the
  slice ends. Looney Tunes is not in the list, and our JIT IDLE SKIP is the
  general form of (2) (0 skips in the Looney Tunes race). Trap for a port:
  its `hash()` reads the code as bytes (`u8* ptr`, `u16 data=ptr[i]`), so
  it hashes the first `guest_opcodes` bytes, each as 2 bytes, and the
  `0xD` reloc mask never acts. Proposed and accepted (Matt: "I'll do the
  JIT HOTBLOCKS run now."): a profile of Looney Tunes at X3 BACKWARD, then
  make its wait loops end the slice (a hash list or a better detector), if
  the extra host time is wait loops.
- **HW run 12, 2026-10-12 ~00:02-00:06: the profile. Looney Tunes, X3
  BACKWARD, JIT HOTBLOCKS ON, JIT BCACHE ON** (`[jitcfg] hotblocks=1 ...
  idlerule=1`; `b8_lt_x3_hot.txt`, 10 censuses, 128 block dumps). Matt:
  "Run's done." Clean JIT EXIT. Race: 90 windows, SPEED 56.2%.
  - **One wait loop takes 46.6% of the JIT's host instructions** (census
    10, 100 dense windows, 101.4 s): the blocks 8C01453E, 8C014544 and
    8C0713D0, 4.67M turns/s each (16.7 + 15.5 + 14.4% of the weight). In
    the X30 profile (`run_prof.txt`, 2026-10-08, session 898d8ac1) the
    same loop ran 43K turns/s, 0.28% of the weight. So at X3 the game ends
    its frame early in emulated time and waits here, 108 times more.
  - The loop: `8C01453E: mov.l @(PC),r0; jsr @r0; mov #6,r4` ->
    `8C0713D0: mov.l @(PC),r0; shll2 r4; add r0,r4; rts; fmov.s @r4,fr0`
    -> `8C014544: ftrc fr0,FPUL; sts FPUL,r1; mov.l @(PC),r0; mov.l
    @r0,r0; cmp/gt r1,r0; bt 8C01453E`. That is `while (*counter >
    (int)table[6]) ;`: the game's own frame wait on a counter in memory. No
    store, 14 ops, 12 billed cycles per turn at every level (none of the
    three blocks falls under the idle rule: jsr and rts ends, FPU ops).
  - So P71's cost in this game is waiting, not game work (the reading of
    run 2, now with a profile). JIT IDLE SKIP does not catch the loop
    (`[idle]` skips/s 0): its candidates are blocks of the idle rule (no
    FPU op, under 6 opcodes), and this loop closes in a block of 6 opcodes
    with `ftrc`. Reicast's small rule misses it for the same reasons.
  - Estimate, not measured: without this loop the X3 race needs between
    0.88 and 1.07 times the host time of the X30 race (the loop's share
    counted in instructions; its time share is not known). So 30 frames/s
    at about full speed is in reach.
  - Two ways, open (Matt's call): (A) widen JIT IDLE SKIP's candidates to
    this shape (a closing block with FPU reads, a few more opcodes; the
    run-time proof stays: no store since the last check, the same
    register hash, plus the block's FPU inputs); general, no list. (B) a
    list of known wait loops as Reicast's `idle_hash`, with this loop as
    its first entry; per game, each new game needs a profile run.

- TMU Clock EFF (6.4): below SH4 Clock 200 a slice counts x 200 / clock in
  the TMU, so the timers keep 50 MHz of Pclk per emulated second. **At SH4
  Clock 200 and above it changes nothing: its HW test needs SH4 Clock
  150.** The TMU now counts in 1/4096 SH4 cycle (`TMU_FRAC` 12,
  `dc/sh4/tmu.cpp`) in every mode. The slice's count is scaled once, with
  no carried remainder, so each slice has the same count and the SYS GATE's
  closed forms (5.36, 5.42) hold. Rate error at 150 MHz: 0.14 ppm or less.
  The rate is latched at a slice update (`tmu_clock_latch()`).
- TMU Fine TCNT (P11, Flycast `b31f92f8e`): a TCNT read adds the SH4
  cycles run inside the slice. The JIT stores `ppc_cycles` in
  `Sh4cntx.jit_cycles` (`emit_cycles_store()`, `ps3/ps3_driver.cpp`, 6
  places): before each cold memory C call, before each interpreter
  fallback, at the loop entry, at each slice end and on both RESUME paths.
  A block takes its cycles at its entry, so the resolution is one block, as
  in Flycast. The read works on a copy: an underflow inside the slice
  gives the reloaded count; UNF and the interrupt come at the slice end
  (Matt's pick). A write that changes a channel (TCNT, TSTR, a new TCR
  prescaler) first commits the cycles run so far (`tmu_commit()`), so a
  write and a read in one slice measure the time between them. A commit
  can set UNF. The interpreter engines keep the slice resolution. With
  SH4 Clock above 200 the SH4's longer slice is scaled to the module slice.
- SPG Field Bit FRAME (P28): `SPG_STATUS.fieldnum` flips once per frame, at
  line 0, as Flycast `spg.cpp:158-163`; LINE flips on each line. HBlank IRQ
  MODES (P28): mode 0 raises `holly_HBLank` at `SPG_HBLANK_INT`'s compare
  line, mode 2 on each line, modes 1 and 3 never (Flycast `spg.cpp:140-155`);
  VBLANK raises one at each vblank. With the reset value (mode 0, line 0)
  MODES moves the interrupt from the vblank line to line 0. A write to
  `SPG_HBLANK_INT` now syncs the SYS GATE (both values). VBLANK INT Reset
  FLYCAST: `SPG_VBLANK_INT` resets to 0x00150104 (SCANINT2 at line 21, not
  336); the BIOS writes the register.

  byte order change. The registers and the end are those of a write. OFF:
  the message box and no end, as before.

  CA. With SPE ARM7 ON (the default since 2026-10-05) the PPU runs no twin:

  SH4 thread tests its writes against the map.
- The rows (options page 2, AUDIO; the key is in `nullDC.cfg` [ps3]). All
  need SPE AICA Sound; the DSP rows need SPE AICA DSP too. `[sndcfg]` shows
  the six keys.

    waits for the sound SPU when a slot has yet to play that byte. Since
    the package of 16:55 also + BLOCK SYNC and + SAMPLE SYNC (top of this
    section).
  - DSP Ring RAM (`DspRingRam`, P20 G2): OFF / ON, set before boot. The
    sound SPU's DSP ring (up to 32K words) is wave RAM for the guest too,
    both ways.
  - DSP Ring 64K (`DspRing64K`, P20 G3): OFF / ON, set before boot. DSP
    writes of a 64K-word ring, and TABLE writes past the ring, reach wave
    RAM.
  - DSP Reg Reads (`DspRegRead`, P20 G4): OFF / ON, set before boot. A read
    of TEMP, MEMS, MIXS or EFREG (0x4000-0x45BF) returns the DSP's value.
  - Mono Mix Fix (`AicaMonoFix`, P31): OFF / ON, set before boot. MONO
    output is (L + R) / 2 (Flycast 136ce267d), in the SPU model and in
    nullAICA's mixer.
  - LFORE Keep (`AicaLfore`, P31): OFF / ON, set before boot. A write to
    the LFO register leaves LFORE set (Flycast 27fd0d426; caique keeps it).
    Only the register read-back changes.
- 6.6, how it works:
  - The map: 1 KB, one bit per 256 bytes of wave RAM. At each CHECK (64
    samples) the twin marks, for each slot that plays, the bytes from the
    sound SPU's play point (its lag + 8 samples behind the twin's CA) to
    256 samples ahead. Loops wrap; a slot with LEA at or below LSA, or with
    CA past LEA, gets all its positions. The model does it
    (`AicaModel::hz_mark`, `hz_hit` in `plugs/caiqueAICA/aica_model.cpp`).
  - The SH4 thread tests each wave RAM write (`aram_hz_write` in
    `libAICA_WriteMem_aica_ram`; a G2 DMA goes the same way). A hit sends
    `ARM_CMD_SYNC` and waits for the ARM7 SPU. That SPU makes the exact
    test of 6.6 (`hz_hit`: the byte is between the sound SPU's play point
    and the twin's). Only then it sends `AICA_OP_SYNC` and waits for the
    sound SPU, which plays up to that sample, then drops its cache. Then
    the write lands. The ARM7 SPU tests its own stores the same way
    (`aram_store`).
  - Limits per 64-sample block: 4 exact tests, 1 sync. More are counted as
    `miss`. After a sync, other writes at the same sample pass free. The
    SH4 also asks when it is more than 192 samples ahead of the map
    (`stale`).
  - No answer from the sound SPU in 50 ms (PPU twin: 100 ms): sync goes
    off for the session (`timeouts`).
  - Always on, as 6.6 says: the sound SPU drops its wave RAM cache at the
    start of each batch of records.
- P20 G2: while a DSP program is set, the LS ring is a copy of the ring in
  wave RAM. The SPU loads it when the program, RBP or RBL changes. At each
  CHECK it writes back the lines (128 bytes) that the round's MWT steps
  wrote (worked out from the program: MADRS + MDEC_CT; an ADRS-relative
  step marks 2048 words each way). A guest write into the ring syncs first
  (the ring's pages are on the map), then goes to the SPU as an
  `AICA_OP_RING` record, and the SPU loads those lines again.
- P20 G3: a DSP write through the line cache marks the line; the SPU puts
  it back before the line leaves the cache (at each CHECK, at a sync, when
  another line takes its place).
- P20 G4: a read sends `AICA_OP_DSPRD` and waits for the sound SPU's value
  (one sync per read). With the row OFF the reads are only counted.
- Where it runs: the twin's side is in `ps3/spu/spe_arm7.cpp` (SPE ARM7 ON)
  and again in `ps3/ps3_aica_spe.cpp` for the PPU twin (SPE ARM7 OFF); the
  SH4 side is in `ps3/ps3_arm_spe.cpp`; the sound SPU's in
  `ps3/spu/spe_aica_model.cpp`, `spe_aica_ram.h`, `spe_aica.c`.
- Cost. Rows OFF: one byte test per SH4 wave RAM write and per ARM7 store.
  Sync: bound by the limits (689 syncs/s at most); 6.6 expects 0.01-0.3%.
  PC, sound SPU, with random DSP programs (much more ring traffic than a
  game: 160 ring lines written back per block): DSP Ring RAM +3.8 points
  of real time (48.4 -> 52.2%), DSP Ring 64K +1.3 points.
- Logs: `[aram-hz]` every ~5 s while a row is on or a count moved (map
  pages, hits by writer sh4 / dma / arm, tests, hazards with their distance
  behind the play point, ring hits and records, syncs/s, miss/s, timeouts,
  sync wait, SH4 wait % of wall, DSP register reads by sh4 / arm, ring and
  cache lines of the SPU); `clip/s=L/R` on the `[aica-spe] sound` line;
  `nullAICA clip L/R` on the `[aicafix]` line. The count of DSP register
  reads works with every row OFF: it tells if a game reads them at all.

- A fact found on the way: the old `run_a2` scenarios never set MVOL, so

- Known limits:
  - A slot that stops inside the lag window has no mark for its last
    bytes. A slot whose loop end moves below its CA walks back in steps;
    the map does not cover that walk once it is over.
  - SPE ARM7 OFF with the ARM7 JIT: the JIT's inline stores are not
    tested (SH4, DMA and interpreter stores are). With Sound Thread ON the
    rows do nothing.
  - A guest write into the ring that gets no sync (over the block's limit)
    wins over DSP writes not yet written back to that 128-byte line.
  - A slot that plays from the ring's memory sees DSP output up to one
    block late.

- The row (`TrTriSort` in `nullDC.cfg` [ps3], live), for a translucent
  list the PVR sorts (autosort):
  - ON: Flycast's default path (`sortTriangles`, `drawSorted`). Each
    strip is cut into triangles (one with an inf corner is left out). The
    key is the farthest corner (the smallest 1/W; ours compares the
    largest W). A stable sort, far to near. The triangles go out as
    GL_TRIANGLES in runs of one state, with no depth write.
  - + DEPTH WRITE: the same sort and draw, but each polygon writes depth
    as the game asks (and as the TR Depth Write row says). Expected: Sonic
    Adventure right; Rayman 2's water not sure.
  - + OPAQUE DEPTH (our own design, no reference): two passes over the
    same sorted triangles. First, depth only: a texel whose alpha is 240
    of 255 or more writes its depth (alpha test, no colour, no blend).
    Then the colour, far to near, with no depth write. A texel that hides
    what is behind it does so in any order (the models); the rest blend
    in the sorted order (the water). It draws the list twice. Only a
    polygon whose blend can hide something is in the first pass (HW run
    3): an additive one is not.
  - In all three: a strip's odd triangles have their first two corners
    swapped, so each triangle winds as its strip does and its newest
    corner stays last (flat shading); a triangle of the other cull
    direction joins the run with the two corners swapped again. A
    presorted list, and the opaque and punch-through lists, do not change.
- Where it runs: the render thread (PPU): `tri_collect`, `tri_sort` (a
  radix sort), `tri_runs` and `draw_tr_tris` in `ps3/ps3_rend.cpp`. With
  SPE Build the request flag `SPEVB_NO_TR` makes the SPU answer TR_PPU at
  once: it builds the opaque and punch-through runs only
  (`spe_vb_build.h`, one SPU image changed). It needs Vertex Arrays and
  Strip Merge (the defaults); without them the sort stays per strip.
- Cost: the PPU writes 3 vertices per triangle into RSX memory, and the
  SPU no longer builds the translucent runs. `[rend] busy=`, `draw split:
  sort`, `[rend4] tris=` (sorted triangles per render), `[spevb] trppu`.
